title: Meeting: presenting and AI support
intro: How each case is shown in the meeting: who controls the screen, what comes first, order and timing, records and images, absent heads' agents and live questions. You liked presenter mode (I01); screen layout comes later in R17.

questions.question: Who should control the shared screen during a case?

options.label: Coordinator, presenter can take over (Recommended)
options.description: The coordinator moves between cases; the case's presenter takes control with one tap for their case and hands it back.

options.label: Presenter drives their case
options.description: Control passes to each case's presenter when their case starts.

options.label: Coordinator only
options.description: The presenter talks; the coordinator clicks everything.

questions.why: I01 liked (presenter mode), G25 (no presenter view today). Today the coordinator moves through the agenda (Make current, D3). Settled: the coordinator runs the board (T19 note).

questions.question: Who should be named presenter of each case?

options.label: Doctor picks at mark-ready (Recommended)
options.description: The treating doctor names themselves or one of the Case File's residents; the name shows on the agenda.

options.label: Always the treating doctor
options.description: Residents help prepare but do not present.

options.label: Decided in the meeting
options.description: Whoever takes the screen presents; nothing named before.

questions.why: Real world: the resident often presents (D3); settled: residents are on the treating doctor's team per Case File. The NCG Virtual Tumour Board template has a 'presenter' field.

questions.question: Should remote members' screens follow the shared screen?

options.label: Follow, can step away (Recommended)
options.description: Their view follows the presenter; they may look at another part of the same case and tap 'back to presenter'.

options.label: Always follow
options.description: They see only what the room sees.

options.label: Browse freely
options.description: They open any part of the agenda's cases themselves.

questions.why: Settled: members join from anywhere, phones included. Hybrid boards (24.8% in India) need remote members to stay on the case being discussed.

questions.question: What should the presenter view show for each case?

options.label: Question for the board (Recommended)
options.description: The one or two lines the doctor wrote saying what the board should decide.

options.label: Key values with sources
options.description: Diagnosis, stage and markers as recorded, each with its verified quote one tap away.

options.label: Gaps and waivers
options.description: Badges for records missing, waived (with the reason) or not final.

options.label: Absent heads' agent points
options.description: The Points for review from each absent head's agent, labelled AI support.

questions.why: I01 liked: one case per screen, large type, the board question, key values with sources one click away, gap badges, a timer. Layout is R17; this is only the content. Stage is only shown as recorded, never computed.

questions.question: What should come first when a case opens on the shared screen?

options.label: Patient line and question (Recommended)
options.description: Age, sex, cancer as recorded and the question for the board; the summary sits below.

options.label: Case File summary
options.description: The cited summary in the six NCG sections, as today.

options.label: Key values
options.description: The main recorded values with their sources.

options.label: Images
options.description: The key study opened in the image viewer.

questions.why: I01; Hartmann 2026: case preparation takes 13 min and the summary is rewritten 3.5 times, so the room needs the point first. CRUK: more than half of cases get 2 minutes or less. If R10-Q06 left the question optional, a case without one shows 'no question written'.

questions.question: In what order should cases be taken on the day?

options.label: Grouped by presenter (Recommended)
options.description: Each team's cases come together so busy doctors can leave after; 'for noting' cases at the end; the coordinator can reorder.

options.label: Most complex first
options.description: The coordinator ranks cases; 'for noting' ones at the end.

options.label: Order marked ready
options.description: First ready, first discussed (close to today's listing order).

questions.why: Today the agenda follows listing order and the coordinator can reorder. I05 triage lists (for discussion, for noting) set by R10-Q11.

questions.question: Should each case show a timer?

options.label: Visible, soft warning (Recommended)
options.description: A 5-minute timer per case changes colour when time is up; nothing stops; time is kept for the minutes.

options.label: Each board sets minutes
options.description: Each board picks its own target (3 to 6 minutes); same soft warning.

options.label: Recorded, not shown (today)
options.description: Time per case is kept for the minutes and the dashboard only.

questions.why: I01 included a case timer. Research: 3 to 6 minutes per case; CRUK 2017: more than half of patients discussed for 2 minutes or less. Time per case is already recorded (12 Oct, board.py timing).

questions.question: Who may open records and images on the shared screen?

options.label: Presenter and coordinator (Recommended)
options.description: Either opens a report or the images (OHIF image viewer through the app, audited); others ask them to.

options.label: Any hospital member joined
options.description: Any joined member with access may put a record or image on the shared screen.

options.label: Coordinator only
options.description: Only the coordinator opens records and images.

questions.why: D3, V2 6.3: records with HIS status and signature, PDF fetched live if missing; images open in OHIF through the app (12 h grant, audited); people view images, no model reads them. K03: grants are lost on restart.

questions.question: When should an absent head's agent come in during a case?

options.label: After the presenter, on a tap (Recommended)
options.description: Once the presenter finishes, the coordinator opens that agent's Points for review, labelled 'AI support, not a board member'.

options.label: Shown from the start
options.description: The agent's points sit beside the case from the first moment.

options.label: Only when asked
options.description: Nothing shows until someone asks the agent a question.

questions.why: D2: every head not recorded present gets its agent per Case File; Eswar (10 Oct): the agent gives its view, the board re-thinks and decides. Scope: Points for review are questions about the records, never findings or treatment.

questions.question: How should an absent head's agent give its points to the room: spoken or as text?

options.label: Text, read aloud on tap (Recommended)
options.description: Points show as text; a speaker button reads that same text aloud (local voice, English first, nothing new said).

options.label: Text only
options.description: Nothing is spoken; the presenter or coordinator reads them out.

options.label: Read aloud automatically
options.description: Each point is spoken when the agent's turn comes.

questions.why: audio_feature.md: text-to-speech (Kokoro-82M, on the H200) reads only text already on screen; units and stage strings need a text normaliser first; researched, not built yet.
questions.skip_if: Skip if R09-Q13 ticked nothing (nothing is read aloud).
questions.notes: Voice deferred (R09-Q13 own words): agent points shown as text only for now.

questions.question: How should live questions to the Case File or an agent be asked in the meeting?

options.label: Text or hold-to-speak (Recommended)
options.description: Type, or hold the mic button and speak; the words land in the box to check before sending; audio is not stored.

options.label: Text only (today)
options.description: Typing only.

options.label: Coordinator asks for the room
options.description: Members say it aloud; the coordinator types or dictates it.

questions.why: D4: Ask the Case File and Ask an agent answer with citations or 'not documented' and refuse out-of-scope questions. audio_feature.md: speech to text runs locally (Whisper large-v3-turbo), English first, spoken text passes the same scope guard as typed text; the microphone needs HTTPS or localhost.
questions.skip_if: Skip if R09-Q12 answered 'Not yet' (no voice input).
questions.notes: Voice deferred (R09-Q13 own words): live questions are typed.

questions.question: Who may ask live questions during the meeting?

options.label: Hospital members joined (Recommended)
options.description: Anyone joined with a Vaidyx login who may read that case; outside experts listen only.

options.label: Presenter and coordinator
options.description: Others ask them to put the question.

options.label: Everyone joined
options.description: Outside experts may ask too.

questions.why: Today any account placed in a department may ask the agents (matrix 'ask'). Outside experts joining by code (R11-Q05) are new.

questions.question: Where should a live answer appear?

options.label: Asker first, then share (Recommended)
options.description: The asker sees the cited answer and can put it on the shared screen with one tap.

options.label: Always on the shared screen
options.description: Every answer shows to the whole room.

options.label: Only to the asker
options.description: Answers never go on the shared screen.

questions.why: Answers take 1.6 to 5.9 s and carry verified quotes (D4); showing them to the asker first keeps the shared screen on the case.

questions.question: What should a member on a phone be able to do during the meeting?

options.label: Follow the current case (Recommended)
options.description: The case's key lines and the agent points, sized for a phone.

options.label: Ask questions
options.description: Text or voice to the Case File or an agent.

options.label: Raise a hand
options.description: A hand shows on the room screen so the coordinator brings them in.

options.label: Open images
options.description: The image viewer on the phone; small screen, every view audited.

questions.why: Settled: members join from anywhere, phones included. U02: phone pages are about 9,500 px tall today. R17 designs the screens; R15 decides patient data on phones.
